title: Release Railroad: Slot Allocator and Backfill Policy for Runtime/Console/API
creator: Marcus Hale
description:
Background: As we scale simultaneous launches across runtime, console, and API surfaces we have recurring contention on limited launch windows and dedicated capacity. Existing ad-hoc slot reservations lead to last-minute rollbacks, uneven operational load, and inability to guarantee SLA coverage for high-risk cutovers. This ticket establishes a deterministic 'Release Railroad'—a slot allocator and backfill policy that schedules launch lanes, enforces guardrails, and automates fallbacks across teams and regions.

Goal: Design and deliver a lightweight slot allocation algorithm + backfill policy that: (1) maps launches to discrete slots (primary / reserve / shadow) in the calendar, (2) reserves minimal capacity per slot with hedging rules, (3) provides automated backfill and preemption rules for canceled or delayed launches, and (4) surfaces clear ownership and rollout signals in the Launch Calendar UI and runbook.

Scope: MVP covers: runtime, console, and public API launches (customer-facing changes and model-serving changes). Out of scope for MVP: on-prem/private deployment cadence (handled by a separate private-deploy schedule), infra-level rolling kernel updates (will be scheduled via infra ops lanes).

Non-goals / Constraints: Must be implementable with existing calendar service and routing metadata; minimal infra changes preferred. The allocator should be transparent and auditable; SLAs remain enforced by Dedicated capacity owners.

Design summary (MVP):
- Slots: 3 slot classes per launch window — Primary (scheduled, 70% capacity allocation), Reserve (hold for spillover, 20%), Shadow (non-production shadow or traffic light test, 10%).
- Preemption policy: Primary can be preempted by higher-priority launches only with 72h notice and approval from slot steward. Reserve auto-promotes to Primary if Primary cancels <48h before the window.
- Backfill: Unused Primary capacity is offered to queued low-risk launches in priority order via the allocator; if no matches, capacity can be released to general pool 24h before window.
- Hedging: At T-7d, the allocator reserves a 10% regional hedging buffer that is released T-1d if unused. This protects against cross-region traffic spikes during cutover.
- Safety gates: Each slot requires a preflight checklist link and owner sign-off in the calendar entry. The calendar will surface 'go/no-go' signal and the associated SLO risk tier.

Deliverables:
- Algorithm spec (doc): deterministic slot scoring, tie-breakers, and promotion rules.
- Calendar UX update spec: slot badges (Primary/Reserve/Shadow), owner, go/no-go toggle, automatic capacity numbers.
- Automation: small service that runs allocation and promotion rules, posts updates to calendar and notifies owners.
- Runbook updates: weekend/region failover, rollback triggers, and cost-hedge steps.

Acceptance criteria:
- Slot allocator algorithm documented and reviewed (Design + Eng sign-off).
- Calendar shows slot assignments for upcoming 12 weeks for runtime/console/api within the new UI layer.
- Automation successfully promotes a Reserve to Primary in a staged test (staging calendar) without manual intervention.
- Backfill process can claim released capacity in end-to-end test and updates calendar + Slack channel.
- Owners and oncall runbook updated and linked from calendar entries.

Metrics to validate success:
- Reduction in last-minute rollbacks caused by slot contention (target: -60% in first 8 weeks).
- Mean time to reassign slot when a Primary cancels (target: <90 minutes after notification).
- Percentage of launches using Reserve -> Primary promotion path (target: 20% of launches).

Stakeholders: ["Lina Chen (PM lead)", "Devon Patel (Runtime eng)", "Haruka Sato (Console PM)", "Ravi Shah (SRE)", "Design: Zoe Park"]
acceptance_criteria: 1) Spec doc reviewed by Eng/Design/Prod; 2) Allocator service deployed to staging with a simulation harness; 3) Calendar UI renders slot states and owner signoffs; 4) Automated promotion/backfill runs in staging and notifies channels; 5) Runbook published and peer-reviewed; 6) Post-launch telemetry dashboard created (slot contention, promotions, rollback counts).
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Over-reservation reduces usable capacity -> Mitigation: dynamic hedging buffer released at T-1d
Risk: Complex tie-breakers create disputes -> Mitigation: deterministic score + escalation path to Release Council
Risk: Automation bug promotes wrong slot -> Mitigation: staged rollout + canary toggles and manual override button
